en.name: Water bamboo
en.summary: Water bamboo is the swollen stem of Manchurian wild rice, sold in its green husks and eaten as a crisp white shoot. Kept in the husk in the fridge it runs about 5–7 days. There is no published Taiwanese figure for it, so that range is borrowed from corn on the cob, another husked grass stem that starts losing sugar and moisture the moment it is cut.
en.pantry: Room temperature is where water bamboo goes woody. Like sweetcorn, it converts sugar and loses water fast once harvested, and a warm kitchen accelerates both. There is no counter-storage figure to give; the honest advice is to get it into the fridge the day you buy it and leave the husks on until you cook.
en.fridge: Leave the green husks on — they are what stops the white stem drying out — and bag the whole shoots in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. About 5–7 days is the working range, borrowed from corn on the cob rather than published for this vegetable. Peel only what you are about to cook; a husked shoot dries and yellows within a day or two. Black specks running through the flesh are the smut fungus that creates the vegetable in the first place, not spoilage, though a heavily blackened stem is past its best.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for water bamboo and raw freezing is a poor idea — the crunch that is the entire appeal turns to mush. If you have a glut, blanch and slice it and use it straight from frozen in a stir-fry or soup, understanding that the texture will be soft. For most households it is better to buy what you will eat within the week.
spoilage: The exposed white stem gone dry, fibrous or yellow-brown at the cut end
Flesh almost entirely black rather than flecked, with a musty smell
Soft, slimy or sunken patches under the husk
Husks that have dried to paper and pulled away from the stem
tips: Buy shoots that feel heavy and firm with fresh green husks still tight around them.
Never peel in advance; the husk is the packaging.
Stand the shoots upright in the crisper so they are not crushed.
A few black specks are normal and harmless — they are the fungus that makes the shoot swell.

faq.q: How long does water bamboo last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 5–7 days with the husks left on. That range is borrowed from corn on the cob; no agency publishes a figure for water bamboo.

faq.q: Are the black spots in water bamboo safe?
faq.a: Yes. They are the smut fungus that causes the stem to swell into the vegetable. A shoot that has gone almost entirely black is simply old.

faq.q: Should you peel water bamboo before storing?
faq.a: No. The husks keep the stem from drying out, so peel only what you are about to cook.
No timeline exists and raw freezing ruins the crunch. Blanch and slice it first if you must, and use it in cooked dishes.

zh.name: 茭白筍
zh.summary: 茭白筍是菰（真菰）膨大的嫩莖，帶著綠殼販售，吃的是裡面那段脆白的芯。連殼冷藏大約可放 5～7 天。台灣目前沒有發表過它的保存天數，這個範圍是比照玉米（帶殼甜玉米）來看的——同樣是帶殼的禾本科莖，採收後就開始流失糖分和水分。
zh.pantry: 室溫是茭白筍變老的地方。和甜玉米一樣，採收後糖分轉化、水分流失都很快，廚房越熱越明顯。這裡沒有常溫天數可以給；誠實的建議是買回來當天就冰，而且下鍋前都不要剝殼。
zh.fridge: 綠殼留著——它就是防止白色筍身乾掉的東西——整支裝袋放進 4 °C 以下的蔬果室，大約 5～7 天。這個範圍是比照玉米來看的，不是針對茭白筍發表的數字。要煮多少才剝多少；剝了殼的筍身一兩天就會乾黃。肉裡的黑點是讓這種蔬菜長成這樣的黑穗菌，不是腐壞，不過整支都黑到發沉的就已經過了賞味期。
zh.freezer: 茭白筍沒有冷凍期限，生凍也不是好主意——它唯一的賣點就是脆，冷凍後會變得軟爛。真的一次買太多，可以汆燙後切片冷凍，直接下鍋炒或煮湯，但要有口感偏軟的心理準備。對大多數家庭來說，買一週內吃得完的量比較實際。
spoilage: 露出的白色筍身乾掉、纖維化，切口轉黃褐
肉幾乎整片發黑而不是點狀分布，並帶有霉味
殼底下有軟爛、黏滑或凹陷的區塊
外殼乾成紙狀、和筍身分離
tips: 挑拿起來有重量、摸起來結實、外殼還青綠緊實的。
不要事先剝殼，殼就是它的包裝。
在蔬果室裡直立擺放，避免被壓傷。
少量黑點是正常且無害的，那正是讓它膨大的菌。

faq.q: 茭白筍放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 連殼冷藏大約 5～7 天。這個範圍是比照玉米來看的，沒有機構為茭白筍發表過數字。

faq.q: 茭白筍裡的黑點可以吃嗎？
faq.a: 可以。那是讓莖膨大成筍的黑穗菌。整支都黑掉的則只是老了。

faq.q: 茭白筍要先剝殼再冰嗎？
faq.a: 不要。殼能防止筍身乾掉，要煮多少再剝多少。
沒有對應期限，生凍會毀掉脆度。真的要冷凍請先汆燙切片，並且只用在熟食裡。
